title: A transdiagnostic framework for neurological intervention in maladaptive repetitive behaviors
title_zh: 跨诊断框架：针对不良重复行为的神经干预
abstract: From daily rituals to pathological patterns of behavior and thought, a wide spectrum of habitual behaviors emerges through repeated reinforcement learning and becomes embedded in cortico-basal ganglia circuits. Once established, these behaviors operate automatically and resist conscious control. This review summarizes neurological intervention strategies for correcting pathological habits (e.g., addiction, obsessive-compulsive disorder) and restoring adaptive behavioral patterns. Pharmacological approaches target the plasticity of habit circuits via modulation of dopamine, serotonin, and glutamate systems. Non-invasive brain stimulation techniques-such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), and deep TMS-can modulate cortical control networks and indirectly influence connected subcortical circuitry. Behavioral interventions include extinction learning, reinforcement of alternative actions, contextual modification, cognitive strategies, and memory reconsolidation-based techniques. Recently, hybrid approaches combining AI-based digital therapeutics (DTx) with neuromodulatory devices have gained attention. Invasive techniques such as optogenetics and deep brain stimulation (DBS) enable direct modulation of specific neural circuits, allowing suppression of habitual responses or facilitation of alternative learning. Beyond clinical applications, these approaches elucidate the neural mechanisms underlying habitual behavior. Modulation of habits is most effective when employing multi-level, combinatorial interventions rather than a single technique. Integrating these strategies, this paper proposes a staged framework-habit circuit suppression → alternative learning → consolidation → sustained management-and a neuroscience-based, personalized model for behavioral treatment with implications for future clinical and research applications.
abstract_zh: 从日常仪式到病理性行为与思维模式，广泛的习惯行为通过重复的强化学习形成，并嵌入皮质-基底神经节回路。一旦建立，这些行为便自动化运行，抵抗意识控制。本综述总结了纠正病理习惯（如成瘾、强迫症）并恢复适应性行为模式的神经干预策略。药物方法通过调节多巴胺、血清素和谷氨酸系统来影响习惯回路的可塑性。非侵入性脑刺激技术——如重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）、经颅直流电刺激（tDCS）和深层TMS——可调节皮质控制网络，并间接影响相关的亚皮质回路。行为干预包括消退学习、强化替代行为、情境修改、认知策略以及基于记忆重巩固的技术。近年来，结合人工智能的数字疗法（DTx）与神经调节装置的混合方法受到关注。侵入性技术如光遗传学和深脑刺激（DBS）可直接调节特定神经回路，抑制习惯性反应或促进替代学习。除临床应用外，这些方法阐明了习惯行为的神经机制。习惯调节在多层次、组合干预下最为有效，而非单一技术。本文整合这些策略，提出了一个分阶段框架——习惯回路抑制 → 替代学习 → 巩固 → 持续管理——以及基于神经科学的个性化行为治疗模型，对未来临床与研究具有重要意义。
